W2 (empirical), after E036. Tip is E036: 5.314 s, 0.7532 on seeds 0-2. That is E035 plus a whitening-bias stop at 20% of steps (a third compiled step variant). It saved 0.131 s (-2.4%) for -0.16 pp on seeds 0-2. The margin over the 0.753 gate is about zero on seeds 0-2. Held-out seeds run about 0.2 pp lower, so the population mean is probably near 0.751-0.752, and the official 0.75 bar is at risk.

Mechanisms, each tied to measured runs:
1. Epoch dial: about 5% of time per 0.5 epoch for 0.0-0.25 pp (E020, E023, E027). Freeze plus 0.5 epoch (E034) gave -0.40 s versus E027 at about 0 pp on seeds 0-2.
2. EMA (+0.97 pp, E005) and Muon (+0.66 pp, confounded, E006) are in the tip. Time-neutral boosters failed 6 times in a row: E025, E029, E030, E032, and the wd and LS variants. Averaging, LR shape and wd are at a flat optimum within noise (about ±0.2 pp).
3. Time tracks pixels. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026, E033). The 28 and 32 px phases carry the accuracy (E018, E024).
4. Backward truncation on memory-bound large maps is the best lever (E028 -0.5 s, E034, E036). Each further stem trim saves 2-3% and costs 0.1-0.2 pp. The returns are shrinking because group 1's backward is already gone for the last 25% of steps.
5. Noise: identical code is bit-identical. Any change to step count or RNG use reshuffles the 3-seed mean by about ±0.2 pp. Time noise is about 0.5%.

Misses: I overpredicted time on trims and freezes (the savings were larger than modelled). I was too optimistic on time-neutral accuracy gains. Accuracy ranges have mostly held.

Unsure: how much margin remains on held-out seeds. Further trims need an accuracy refund, which costs epochs, and that eats the time saved. The tip is probably near the Pareto front for this architecture. Muon-to-SGD is uncertain, and E006 suggests losing Muon costs accuracy.

forecasts.reason: An earlier freeze trims about 2-3% of time (the truncated 28 px steps are cheaper). It likely costs about 0.1 pp, which leaves the result at or below the gate.
There is no recipe change, so time is unchanged. Fresh seeds will likely land near 0.752, the same as the held-out mean, which is just above the 0.75 bar.
Folding the BN into the conv removes memory-bound passes on the 31×31 maps for 25% of steps, which saves about 1.5%. It adds fold complexity and shifts the RNG.
It is a diagnostic with no recipe change. Profiling will most likely show the non-GEMM share at 30% or more, which fits the E028 saving.
Plain SGD should save a little time because the Newton-Schulz cost goes away. The accuracy is likely to drop 0.2-0.5 pp, since Muon's gain on this recipe looks real.

cruxes: What is the true population mean accuracy of the tip on fresh seeds? If it is below 0.751, every further trim needs an accuracy refund first.
What share of a 32 px step is memory-bound large-map work in group 1? This sets the value of BN folding and an earlier freeze.
Does Muon account for most of E006's +0.66 pp? That decides whether the optimizer swap is worth running.
